# telnyx_ai_assistant (Resource)

An AI assistant that handles voice calls, messages and web chats.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "telnyx_ai_assistant" "front_desk" {
  name         = "Front desk"
  instructions = "You answer questions about our opening hours and book appointments."
  greeting     = "Hello, how can I help?"
  tool_ids     = [telnyx_ai_tool.order_status.id]

  voice_settings = {
    voice = "Telnyx.NaturalHD.astra"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instructions` (String) System instructions for the assistant. These may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables)
- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `a2a_agents` (Attributes List) A2A agents this assistant can delegate to. Tools are not stored here: at the start of every conversation each agent's card is fetched and one tool is derived per skill the card advertises, named `a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`. The following limits are not enforced when the assistant is saved, and anything past them is dropped when the conversation starts: 64 agents per assistant, 64 skills per card, 128 derived tools per assistant, and a 6 second budget for all card fetches combined. An agent whose card cannot be fetched costs the assistant that capability for the conversation; it does not fail the call. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--a2a_agents))
- `avatar_settings` (Attributes) **Beta:** Saved avatar configuration for supported realtime browser conversations. `null` means that no avatar is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--avatar_settings))
- `conversation_flow` (String) Conversation flow as returned by the API. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `delegation_settings` (Attributes) Splits the conversation between a frontend model that talks to the caller and a backend model that does the work. On the GPT-Live route the frontend model cannot call tools at all — when it needs something done it raises a delegation and waits. On the chat completion route the frontend keeps a single `delegate` tool that returns immediately, so the conversation carries on while the backend works. Either way the backend's answer is spoken as commentary or kept as silent context, depending on `speak_results`. Beta feature. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--delegation_settings))
- `description` (String)
- `dynamic_variables` (String) Map of dynamic variables and their values A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `dynamic_variables_webhook_timeout_ms` (Number) Timeout in milliseconds for the dynamic variables webhook. Must be between 1 and 10000 ms. If the webhook does not respond within this timeout, the call proceeds with default values. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables).
- `dynamic_variables_webhook_url` (String) If `dynamic_variables_webhook_url` is set, Telnyx sends a POST request to this URL at the start of the conversation to resolve dynamic variables. **Gotcha:** the webhook response must wrap variables under a top-level `dynamic_variables` object, e.g. `{"dynamic_variables": {"customer_name": "Jane"}}`. Returning a flat object will be ignored and variables will fall back to their defaults. See the [dynamic variables guide](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) for the full request/response format and timeout behavior.
- `enabled_features` (List of String)
- `external_llm` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--external_llm))
- `fallback_config` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--fallback_config))
- `greeting` (String) Text that the assistant will use to start the conversation. This may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables). Use an empty string to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first. Use the special value `<assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message>` to have the assistant generate the greeting based on the system instructions.
- `insight_settings` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--insight_settings))
- `integrations` (Attributes List) Connected integrations attached to the assistant. The catalog of available integrations is at `/ai/integrations`; the user's connected integrations are at `/ai/integrations/connections`. Each item references a catalog integration by `integration_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--integrations))
- `interruption_settings` (Attributes) Settings for interruptions and how the assistant decides the user has finished speaking. These timings are most relevant when using non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn behavior is controlled by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` (`eot_threshold`, `eot_timeout_ms`, `eager_eot_threshold`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interruption_settings))
- `llm_api_key_ref` (String) This is only needed when using third-party inference providers selected by `model`. The `identifier` for an integration secret [/v2/integration_secrets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/integration-secrets/create-a-secret) that refers to your LLM provider's API key. For bring-your-own endpoint authentication, use `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead. Warning: Free plans are unlikely to work with this integration.
- `mcp_servers` (Attributes List) MCP servers attached to the assistant. Create MCP servers with `/ai/mcp_servers`, then reference them by `id` here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mcp_servers))
- `messaging_settings` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--messaging_settings))
- `model` (String) ID of the model to use when `external_llm` is not set. You can use the [Get models API](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/openai-chat/get-available-models-openai-compatible) to see available models. If `external_llm` is provided, the assistant uses `external_llm` instead of this field. If neither `model` nor `external_llm` is provided, Telnyx applies the default model.
- `observability_settings` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--observability_settings))
- `post_conversation_settings` (Attributes) Configuration for post-conversation processing. When enabled, the assistant receives one additional LLM turn after the conversation ends, allowing it to execute final tool calls such as sending a summary or updating a record via webhook or function tools. Integration and MCP server tools are not available post-conversation; call-control tools (e.g. hangup, transfer) are also unavailable. Beta feature. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--post_conversation_settings))
- `privacy_settings` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--privacy_settings))
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags associated with the assistant. Tags can also be managed with the assistant tag endpoints.
- `telephony_settings` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--telephony_settings))
- `tool_ids` (List of String) IDs of shared tools to attach to the assistant. New integrations should prefer `tool_ids` over inline `tools`. The API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `tools` (Attributes List) Deprecated for new integrations. Inline tool definitions available to the assistant. Prefer `tool_ids` to attach shared tools created with the AI Tools endpoints. On update, a sent `tools` array fully replaces the assistant's inline tools; omit the field to leave them unchanged. Each tool type except `function`, `webhook`, and `client_side_tool` allows at most one instance per assistant, counted across inline `tools` and shared `tool_ids` combined. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools))
- `transcription` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transcription))
- `version_name` (String) Human-readable name for the assistant version.
- `voice_settings` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--voice_settings))
- `websocket_settings` (Attributes) Streams conversation and telephony events to a WebSocket server you host, and accepts messages injected back into the conversation. Telnyx opens the connection as a client, once per conversation. Delivery is best effort throughout: while the connection is down events are dropped rather than queued, and no socket failure is ever allowed to affect the call. Beta feature. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--websocket_settings))
- `widget_settings` (Attributes) Configuration settings for the assistant's web widget. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--widget_settings))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The object's id.
- `import_metadata` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--import_metadata))
- `related_mission_ids` (List of String) IDs of missions related to this assistant.
- `version_created_at` (String) Timestamp when this assistant version was created.
- `version_id` (String) Identifier for the assistant version returned by version-aware assistant endpoints.

<a id="nestedatt--a2a_agents"></a>
### Nested Schema for `a2a_agents`

Optional:

- `async` (Boolean) When `true`, the assistant hands the turn straight back to the model and the agent's answer is delivered into the conversation once it arrives, instead of the caller waiting for it in silence.
- `headers` (Attributes List) Headers sent when fetching this agent's card and on every call made to it. Use them to authenticate to the agent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--a2a_agents--headers))
- `messages` (Attributes List) Filler messages spoken while a call to this agent is in progress. `request_start` messages are spoken immediately when the call begins. `request_response_delayed` messages are spoken after `timing_ms` has elapsed only if the agent has not answered yet. Filler messages are not used when `async` is `true`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--a2a_agents--messages))
- `name` (String) Identifies the agent and seeds the names of the tools derived from its card (`a2a_<name>_<skill_id>`). Characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` are replaced with `_` before the tool name is built, so two agents whose names differ only in punctuation collide and are rejected.
- `poll_interval_ms` (Number) How often, in milliseconds, to poll an agent task that has not finished yet. Defaults to 500.
- `timeout_ms` (Number) Total budget, in milliseconds, for one call to this agent, including any time spent polling a task that is still running. Omit to inherit the assistant's tool timeout.
- `url` (String) The agent's base URL, or the URL of its agent card. At most 2,048 bytes once UTF-8 encoded. `/.well-known/agent-card.json` is appended to the path unless it already ends in `.json`. Must be an `http://` or `https://` URL for an externally reachable host: internal destinations (`localhost`, private and reserved IP ranges, `.local` domains) are rejected, and the hostname may not contain a `{{...}}` placeholder. Placeholders in the path are allowed.

<a id="nestedatt--a2a_agents--headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `a2a_agents.headers`

Optional:

- `name` (String) HTTP header name. May only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores, or a `{{dynamic_variable}}` placeholder surrounded by those characters.
- `value` (String) Header value, stored exactly as written. It may be a literal, a `{{dynamic_variable}}`, or an `{{#integration_secret}}identifier{{/integration_secret}}` section that resolves to a stored integration secret when the conversation starts. Control characters are not allowed. The encrypted `{{variable | encryption_secret_ref}}` form used for per-caller credentials is not resolved here and is rejected when the assistant is saved.


<a id="nestedatt--a2a_agents--messages"></a>
### Nested Schema for `a2a_agents.messages`

Optional:

- `content` (String) The text the assistant speaks.
- `timing_ms` (Number) How long to wait, in milliseconds, before speaking this message.
- `type` (String) One of `request_response_delayed`, `request_start`.



<a id="nestedatt--avatar_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `avatar_settings`

Optional:

- `avatar_id` (String) Stable identifier returned by the Avatars API. Discover available stock IDs with GET /v2/ai/avatars and filter[avatar_type]=stock rather than maintaining a fixed list. Custom avatar IDs use the `avatar_` prefix and must belong to the authenticated organization. The service validates that the selected avatar is available.
- `background_id` (String) The background to render. One of `illustrated_workspace`, `office`, `reception`, `studio`.
- `model` (String) Required avatar model identifier, separate from `avatar_id`. The supported value is `foxtrot-1`. Omission, null, and unsupported model identifiers are rejected. One of `foxtrot-1`.
- `provider` (String) Selects the Telnyx open-source avatar provider.


<a id="nestedatt--delegation_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `delegation_settings`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the assistant delegates work to a backend model. Defaults to `true`: a GPT-Live assistant with delegation disabled can hold a conversation but can never look anything up or run a tool.
- `external_llm` (Attributes) Run the backend on your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of a Telnyx-hosted model. As above, a raw `api_key` here is rejected — reference an integration secret with `external_llm.llm_api_key_ref` instead. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--delegation_settings--external_llm))
- `instructions` (String) Extra instructions for the backend model, in addition to the assistant's own. Use this for the business rules the backend needs and the talking model does not.
- `llm_api_key_ref` (String) Integration secret identifier for the backend model's API key. Required for models from providers other than Telnyx, OpenAI and Anthropic. A raw `api_key` is rejected rather than ignored, so that no plaintext credential is stored on the assistant.
- `mode` (String) Who answers a delegation. `telnyx` runs the backend model on Telnyx with the assistant's own tools, MCP servers and observability. `client` relays the delegation to a server you host over the WebSocket configured in `websocket_settings`: Telnyx sends a `session.delegation.created` frame and waits for your `session.delegation.completed` answer. That answer is text only, since the socket offers no tool vocabulary. If no socket is connected the delegation is refused and the assistant tells the caller it cannot look things up right now. Defaults to `telnyx`. One of `client`, `telnyx`.
- `model` (String) The backend model that answers delegations. Must be a model available for AI Assistants. When enabling `telnyx` delegation, explicitly set this field or `external_llm.model`; a configuration without either backend model is rejected. Only applies when `mode` is `telnyx`.
- `speak_results` (Boolean) Whether the backend's answer is spoken to the caller. When `true` the result is appended as commentary and paraphrased aloud; when `false` it is kept as silent context that informs later answers without being read out. Defaults to `true`.

<a id="nestedatt--delegation_settings--external_llm"></a>
### Nested Schema for `delegation_settings.external_llm`

Optional:

- `authentication_method` (String) Authentication method used when connecting to the external LLM endpoint. One of `certificate`, `token`.
- `base_url` (String) Base URL for the external LLM endpoint.
- `certificate_ref` (String) Integration secret identifier for the client certificate used with certificate authentication.
- `forward_metadata` (Boolean) When `true`, Telnyx forwards the assistant's dynamic variables to the external LLM endpoint as a top-level `extra_metadata` object on the chat completion request body. Defaults to `false`. Example payload sent to the external endpoint: `{"extra_metadata": {"customer_name": "Jane", "account_id": "acct_789", "telnyx_agent_target": "+13125550100", "telnyx_end_user_target": "+13125550123"}}`. Distinct from OpenAI's native `metadata` field, which has its own size and type limits.
- `llm_api_key_ref` (String) Integration secret identifier for the external LLM API key.
- `model` (String) Model identifier to use with the external LLM endpoint.
- `token_retrieval_url` (String) URL used to retrieve an access token when certificate authentication is enabled.

<a id="nestedatt--insight_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `insight_settings`

Optional:

- `insight_group_id` (String) Reference to an Insight Group. Insights in this group will be run automatically for all the assistant's conversations.
- `model` (String) The model that generates the assistant's insights when a conversation ends. It runs every insight in the group, Telnyx-managed insights included. Must be `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` or `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`; any other model returns `422`. When omitted on create, it defaults to `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`; when omitted on update, the current model is kept. `null` uses Telnyx's default insight models, which assistants created before this setting have. Insights of messaging conversations, and insights regenerated later, always use Telnyx's default insight models.


<a id="nestedatt--integrations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `integrations`

Optional:

- `allowed_list` (List of String) Optional per-assistant allowlist of integration tool names. When omitted or empty, all tools allowed by the connected integration are available to the assistant.
- `integration_id` (String) Catalog integration ID to attach. This is the `id` from the integrations catalog at `/ai/integrations` (the same value also appears as `integration_id` on entries returned by `/ai/integrations/connections`). It is **not** the connection-level `id` from `/ai/integrations/connections`.


<a id="nestedatt--interruption_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interruption_settings`

Optional:

- `disable_greeting_interruption` (Boolean) When true, disables user interruptions while the assistant greeting is playing.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether users can interrupt the assistant while it is speaking.
- `interrupt_prediction_threshold` (Number) Interrupt-prediction sensitivity, from 0.0 to 1.0. Set to null or 0.0 to disable interrupt prediction.
- `start_speaking_plan` (Attributes) Controls when the assistant starts speaking after the user stops. These thresholds primarily apply to non turn-taking transcription models. For turn-taking models like `deepgram/flux`, end-of-turn detection is driven by the transcription end-of-turn settings under `transcription.settings` instead. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interruption_settings--start_speaking_plan))

<a id="nestedatt--interruption_settings--start_speaking_plan"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interruption_settings.start_speaking_plan`

Optional:

- `transcription_endpointing_plan` (Attributes) Endpointing thresholds used to decide when the user has finished speaking. Applies to non turn-taking transcription models. For `deepgram/flux`, use `transcription.settings.eot_threshold` / `eot_timeout_ms` / `eager_eot_threshold`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interruption_settings--start_speaking_plan--transcription_endpointing_plan))
- `wait_seconds` (Number) Minimum seconds to wait before the assistant starts speaking.

<a id="nestedatt--interruption_settings--start_speaking_plan--transcription_endpointing_plan"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interruption_settings.start_speaking_plan.transcription_endpointing_plan`

Optional:

- `on_no_punctuation_seconds` (Number) Seconds to wait after the transcript ends without punctuation.
- `on_number_seconds` (Number) Seconds to wait after the transcript ends with a number.
- `on_punctuation_seconds` (Number) Seconds to wait after the transcript ends with punctuation.

<a id="nestedatt--post_conversation_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `post_conversation_settings`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether post-conversation processing is enabled. When true, the assistant will be invoked after the conversation ends to perform any final tool calls. Defaults to false.


<a id="nestedatt--privacy_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `privacy_settings`

Optional:

- `data_retention` (Boolean) If true, conversation history and insights will be stored. If false, they will not be stored. This in‑tool toggle governs solely the retention of conversation history and insights via the AI assistant. It has no effect on any separate recording, transcription, or storage configuration that you have set at the account, number, or application level. All such external settings remain in force regardless of your selection here.
- `in_transit_data_locality` (Boolean) Requires this assistant's conversations to be processed inside your organization's data-locality region, rather than only stored there, on every channel: for web chat, every model call of a turn; for voice, the call's model calls and the Telnyx-hosted speech services it uses; for SMS and WhatsApp, the model calls of each turn (how messages travel through carriers is not covered). Covered processing that cannot be handled in region fails rather than being served elsewhere. Enabling it requires a data-locality region with in-region inference (USA, EU, AUS, UAE; see [Inference regions](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/models/regions)), Telnyx-hosted models for the assistant, its fallback, and any conversation-flow node that overrides the model, and, when `insight_settings.model` is set, an insight model available in that region; the request is rejected otherwise. A voice call fails when it starts if its STT model or TTS voice is not self-hosted by Telnyx, if the assistant uses a speech-to-speech model, or if the call's media is anchored outside the region. Once enabled, send web chat requests and WebSocket or WebRTC conversations to your region's API hostname: one entering the platform in another region is refused rather than forwarded, because forwarding it would already have moved the content across the border. See [Data residency](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/data-residency#in-region-processing-for-ai-assistants). Defaults to false.
- `pii_redaction` (String) Controls redaction of personally identifiable information (PII) from the conversation history that is stored for this assistant. `disabled` (default) stores content as-is. `redact` replaces detected PII with `<PII:type/>` placeholders (e.g. `<PII:name/>`, `<PII:phone/>`) as the stored copies are written: message content (user, assistant, and tool-result messages) and tool-call arguments are redacted when written to conversation history, so the stored transcript, its read-back via the history API, and any insights generated from the stored messages contain the placeholders instead of the PII; response bodies returned by webhook tools are redacted too, as stored in the webhook logs — a per-conversation record separate from the transcript. In the Mission Control Portal this field appears as a "PII Redaction" on/off toggle, where Enabled corresponds to `redact`. Redaction runs when the stored copy is written, after the LLM has generated its reply: the live conversation is not redacted, the assistant's tools keep receiving the full (unredacted) values during the call, and the LLM still sees full content in its context window. Call recordings (including any recording layout configured under telephony settings) and the payloads of messages/webhooks delivered during the call are never redacted by this setting. The set of detected PII types (names, street addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, government identifiers like SSN and driver's license numbers, credit card and bank account numbers, IP addresses, dates of birth, and other identifiers unique to a person) is fixed by Telnyx and cannot be configured or extended per assistant. Assistants with `redact` cannot be used for SMS/WhatsApp messaging (that combination is rejected with a 400 error); voice and web chat are unaffected. One of `disabled`, `redact`.


<a id="nestedatt--telephony_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `telephony_settings`

Optional:

- `conversation_ended_full_history` (Boolean) When enabled, the `messages` array of the `call.conversation.ended` webhook contains the full conversation history in order: user and assistant turns, assistant tool calls (`tool_calls`), tool results (`role: tool` with `tool_call_id`), and informational `system` and `developer` entries. The assistant's instructions are never included. When disabled, `messages` contains only user and assistant text turns.
- `default_texml_app_id` (String) Default Texml App used for voice calls with your assistant. This will be created automatically on assistant creation.
- `disable_dtmf` (Boolean) Disable inbound DTMF for the entire call. Must be set to true if a 'pay' tool is configured anywhere on the assistant — on the main tool array or on any workflow node — enforced at write time.
- `fallback_destination` (String) Destination number or SIP URI to transfer the caller to when the AI conversation ends abnormally, for example because of an assistant-side error, so the caller is not left in dead air. This only fires for abnormal ends: it does not fire when the conversation ends on purpose (the caller hung up, the assistant completed normally, the caller hung up after a relay handoff, or voicemail was detected), and it does not fire when the assistant already transferred or bridged the call.
- `greeting_delay_ms` (Number) Milliseconds to wait after an inbound call is answered before the assistant starts and speaks its greeting. Increase it if the beginning of the greeting is cut off on some connections (for example, WebRTC calls). When unset (`null`), the platform default of 250 ms is used. Set to `0` to start without a delay. Maximum 2000.
- `noise_suppression` (String) The noise suppression engine to use. 'aicoustics' is STT-optimized and recommended for AI assistants (configure through noise_suppression_config). Use 'disabled' to turn off noise suppression. One of `aicoustics`, `deepfilternet`, `disabled`, `krisp`.
- `noise_suppression_config` (Attributes) Configuration for noise suppression. Applicable fields depend on the engine: 'attenuation_limit' and 'mode' only when noise_suppression is 'deepfilternet'; 'family', 'size' and 'enhancement_level' only when noise_suppression is 'aicoustics'. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--telephony_settings--noise_suppression_config))
- `recording_settings` (Attributes) Configuration for call recording format and channel settings. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--telephony_settings--recording_settings))
- `send_message_history_updates` (Boolean) Whether the assistant sends a `call.ai_gather.message_history_updated` webhook with the full message history every time the conversation history changes. Leave unset to inherit the `send_message_history_updates` value from the `ai_assistant_start` or `gather_using_ai` command that started the conversation. Setting it here is authoritative: `true` turns the webhooks on even when the start command did not request them, and `false` turns them off even when it did. Messages exchanged during a private warm transfer acceptance phase are never included.
- `supports_unauthenticated_web_calls` (Boolean) When enabled, allows users to interact with your AI assistant directly from your website without requiring authentication. This is required for FE widgets that work with assistants that have telephony enabled.
- `time_limit_secs` (Number) Maximum duration in seconds for the AI assistant to participate on the call. When this limit is reached the assistant will be stopped. Stopping the assistant does not itself hang up the call, and what happens next depends on how the assistant is running. On Call Control (ai_assistant_start) the call leg stays connected and continues to be billed until it is hung up (for example with the Hangup call command) or until the call ends for another reason. On TeXML, the assistant's `<Connect><AIAssistant>` instruction ends; in the default TeXML setup for assistants no instructions follow it, so the call is hung up. Your application receives a call.conversation.ended webhook when the assistant stops. This limit does not apply to portions of a call without an active assistant (for instance, a call transferred to a human representative).
- `user_idle_reply_secs` (Number) Duration in seconds of end user silence before the assistant checks in on the user. When this limit is reached the assistant will prompt the user to respond. This is distinct from user_idle_timeout_secs which stops the assistant entirely.
- `user_idle_timeout_secs` (Number) Maximum duration in seconds of end user silence on the call. When this limit is reached the assistant will be stopped. Stopping the assistant does not itself hang up the call, and what happens next depends on how the assistant is running. On Call Control (ai_assistant_start) the call leg stays connected and continues to be billed until it is hung up (for example with the Hangup call command) or until the call ends for another reason. On TeXML, the assistant's `<Connect><AIAssistant>` instruction ends; in the default TeXML setup for assistants no instructions follow it, so the call is hung up. Your application receives a call.conversation.ended webhook when the assistant stops. This limit does not apply to portions of a call without an active assistant (for instance, a call transferred to a human representative).
- `voicemail_detection` (Attributes) Configuration for voicemail detection (AMD - Answering Machine Detection) on outgoing calls. These settings only apply if AMD is enabled on the Dial command. See [TeXML Dial documentation](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/texml-rest-commands/initiate-an-outbound-call) for enabling AMD. Recommended settings: MachineDetection=Enable, AsyncAmd=true, DetectionMode=Premium. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--telephony_settings--voicemail_detection))

<a id="nestedatt--telephony_settings--noise_suppression_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `telephony_settings.noise_suppression_config`

Optional:

- `attenuation_limit` (Number) Attenuation limit for noise suppression. Range: 0-100. Only applicable when noise_suppression is 'deepfilternet'.
- `enhancement_level` (Number) AiCoustics enhancement intensity. Range: 0-1. Only applicable when noise_suppression is 'aicoustics'.
- `family` (String) AiCoustics model family optimized for Voice AI and STT. Only applicable when noise_suppression is 'aicoustics'. One of `quail`.
- `mode` (String) Mode for noise suppression configuration. Only applicable when noise_suppression is 'deepfilternet'. One of `advanced`.
- `size` (String) AiCoustics model size. 'vf' tracks the latest model release; 'vf_2_0_l' is pinned to version 2.0 for consistent, predictable behavior. Only applicable when noise_suppression is 'aicoustics'. One of `vf`, `vf_2_0_l`.


<a id="nestedatt--telephony_settings--recording_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `telephony_settings.recording_settings`

Optional:

- `channels` (String) The number of channels for the recording. 'single' for mono, 'dual' for stereo. One of `dual`, `single`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether call recording is enabled. When set to false, calls will not be recorded regardless of other recording configuration.
- `format` (String) The format of the recording file. One of `mp3`, `wav`.
- `stop_on_conversation_end` (Boolean) When enabled, the call recording will stop when the conversation ends (for example, when the assistant hangs up or the call is transferred). When disabled, recording continues until the call itself ends.


<a id="nestedatt--telephony_settings--voicemail_detection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `telephony_settings.voicemail_detection`

Optional:

- `on_voicemail_detected` (Attributes) Action to take when voicemail is detected. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--telephony_settings--voicemail_detection--on_voicemail_detected))

<a id="nestedatt--telephony_settings--voicemail_detection--on_voicemail_detected"></a>
### Nested Schema for `telephony_settings.voicemail_detection.on_voicemail_detected`

Optional:

- `action` (String) The action to take when voicemail is detected. One of `continue_assistant`, `leave_message_and_stop_assistant`, `stop_assistant`.
- `voicemail_message` (String) Configuration for the voicemail message to leave. Only applicable when action is 'leave_message_and_stop_assistant'. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.




<a id="nestedatt--tools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools`

Optional:

- `client_side_tool` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--client_side_tool))
- `function` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--function))
- `handoff` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--handoff))
- `hangup` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--hangup))
- `invite` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--invite))
- `pay` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--pay))
- `refer` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--refer))
- `retrieval` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--retrieval))
- `send_dtmf` (String) A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `send_message` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--send_message))
- `skip_turn` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--skip_turn))
- `timeout_ms` (Number) The maximum number of milliseconds to wait for the webhook to respond before the tool call is aborted. Set this at the tool level, as a sibling of `type` — a `timeout_ms` nested inside the `webhook` object is stored but not applied, and the tool runs at this default instead. Applies when `webhook.async` is false.
- `transfer` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--transfer))
- `type` (String) One of `client_side_tool`, `function`, `handoff`, `hangup`, `invite`, `pay`, `refer`, `retrieval`, `send_dtmf`, `send_message`, `skip_turn`, `transfer`, `update_dynamic_variables`, `vision`, `webhook`.
- `update_dynamic_variables` (Attributes) Configuration for an update_dynamic_variables tool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--update_dynamic_variables))
- `vision` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--vision))
- `webhook` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--webhook))

Read-Only:

- `shared` (Boolean) Whether this tool comes from the shared Tools Library. Responses merge shared tools into `tools` with `shared: true`; inline tools carry `shared: false`. Read-only: set by the server, not accepted in requests. When updating an assistant, omit `shared: true` tools from the request `tools` array and manage them through `tool_ids` instead — re-sending their definitions creates an inline duplicate (rejected with error code 10015 when the type allows only one instance per assistant).

<a id="nestedatt--tools--client_side_tool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.client_side_tool`

Optional:

- `description` (String) The description of the tool.
- `name` (String) The name of the tool.
- `parameters` (Attributes) The parameters the tool accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--client_side_tool--parameters))

<a id="nestedatt--tools--client_side_tool--parameters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.client_side_tool.parameters`

Optional:

- `properties` (String) The properties of the parameters. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `required` (List of String) The required properties of the parameters.
- `type` (String) One of `object`.



<a id="nestedatt--tools--function"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.function`

Optional:

- `description` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `parameters` (String) A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--handoff"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.handoff`

Optional:

- `ai_assistants` (Attributes List) List of possible assistants that can receive a handoff. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--handoff--ai_assistants))
- `voice_mode` (String) With the unified voice mode all assistants share the same voice, making the handoff transparent to the user. With the distinct voice mode all assistants retain their voice configuration, providing the experience of a conference call with a team of assistants. One of `distinct`, `unified`.

<a id="nestedatt--tools--handoff--ai_assistants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.handoff.ai_assistants`

Optional:

- `id` (String) The ID of the assistant to hand off to.
- `name` (String) Helpful name for giving context on when to handoff to the assistant.



<a id="nestedatt--tools--hangup"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.hangup`

Optional:

- `description` (String) The description of the function that will be passed to the assistant.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--invite"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.invite`

Optional:

- `custom_headers` (Attributes List) Custom headers to be added to the SIP INVITE for the invite command. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--invite--custom_headers))
- `from` (String) Number or SIP URI placing the call.
- `targets` (String) The different possible targets of the invite. The assistant will be able to choose one of the targets to invite to the call. This can also be a dynamic variable string like `{{ targets }}` where `targets` is returned by the dynamic variables webhook and resolves to an array of target objects at runtime. If omitted or null, the invite tool can still be configured and targets may be supplied dynamically at runtime. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `voicemail_detection` (Attributes) Configuration for voicemail detection (AMD - Answering Machine Detection) on the invited call. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--invite--voicemail_detection))

<a id="nestedatt--tools--invite--custom_headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.invite.custom_headers`

Optional:

- `name` (String)
- `value` (String) The value of the header. Note that we support mustache templating for the value. For example you can use `{{#integration_secret}}test-secret{{/integration_secret}}` to pass the value of the integration secret.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--invite--voicemail_detection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.invite.voicemail_detection`

Optional:

- `detection_mode` (String) The AMD detection mode to use. 'premium' enables premium answering machine detection. 'disabled' turns off AMD detection. One of `disabled`, `premium`.
- `on_voicemail_detected` (String) Action to take when voicemail is detected on the invited call. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.



<a id="nestedatt--tools--pay"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.pay`

Optional:

- `connector_name` (String) The name of the pay connector configured in the Telnyx API. Must reference an existing pay connector for this organization.
- `connector_parameters` (String) Custom key/value parameters forwarded to the pay connector as `parameters` in the processor request. String values may use `{{dynamic_variable}}` templating, resolved per call. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `currency` (String) Default currency for payments processed by this tool.
- `description` (String) Description of the pay tool shown to the assistant so it knows when to call the tool. Not sent to the payment connector — the per-call `description` argument the assistant passes is what reaches the processor.
- `inter_digit_timeout_millis` (Number) Time in milliseconds to wait between consecutive DTMF digits. Omitted means the platform default (5000) applies.
- `max_attempts` (Number) Maximum number of attempts for each payment collection step. Omitted means the platform default (3) applies.
- `min_postal_code_length` (Number) Minimum number of digits the caller must enter when collecting a credit-card billing postal code. Applies only when `postal_code` prompts the caller. Omitted means the platform default (1) applies. The maximum number of digits collected is the greater of 10 and this value. This does not validate the length of a postal code supplied directly in `postal_code`.
- `payment_method` (String) Default payment method for payments processed by this tool.
- `postal_code` (String) Controls billing postal code collection for credit-card payments. Set to `false` to skip the postal code prompt without supplying a postal code to the payment connector (non-US cards, e.g. Irish Eircodes). Set to `true` to prompt the caller. Supply a non-empty string, such as `"90210"`, to use that postal code without prompting. This option does not affect ACH debit payments or payments using an existing token. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `prompts` (Attributes) Custom text-to-speech prompts keyed by payment collection step. The AI assistant merges its own card-number prompt into this map, matching on the same step keys. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--pay--prompts))
- `timeout_millis` (Number) Time in milliseconds to wait for DTMF input for each collection step. Omitted means the platform default (5000) applies. Increase this for slower entry, e.g. a 16-digit card number.
- `valid_card_types` (List of String) Restricts accepted card numbers to the listed card types. When the caller enters a card number that does not match one of the listed types, Pay treats the input as invalid and re-prompts for the card number.

<a id="nestedatt--tools--pay--prompts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.pay.prompts`

Optional:

- `bank_account_number` (String) A default prompt string or an ordered list of qualified prompts. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `bank_routing_number` (String) A default prompt string or an ordered list of qualified prompts. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `expiration_date` (String) A default prompt string or an ordered list of qualified prompts. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `payment_card_number` (String) A default prompt string or an ordered list of qualified prompts. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `postal_code` (String) A default prompt string or an ordered list of qualified prompts. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `security_code` (String) A default prompt string or an ordered list of qualified prompts. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.



<a id="nestedatt--tools--refer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.refer`

Optional:

- `custom_headers` (Attributes List) Custom headers to be added to the SIP REFER. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--refer--custom_headers))
- `sip_headers` (Attributes List) SIP headers to be added to the SIP REFER. Currently only User-to-User and Diversion headers are supported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--refer--sip_headers))
- `targets` (Attributes List) The different possible targets of the SIP refer. The assistant will be able to choose one of the targets to refer the call to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--refer--targets))

<a id="nestedatt--tools--refer--custom_headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.refer.custom_headers`

Optional:

- `name` (String)
- `value` (String) The value of the header. Note that we support mustache templating for the value. For example you can use `{{#integration_secret}}test-secret{{/integration_secret}}` to pass the value of the integration secret.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--refer--sip_headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.refer.sip_headers`

Optional:

- `name` (String) One of `Diversion`, `User-to-User`.
- `value` (String) The value of the header. Note that we support mustache templating for the value. For example you can use `{{#integration_secret}}test-secret{{/integration_secret}}` to pass the value of the integration secret.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--refer--targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.refer.targets`

Optional:

- `name` (String) The name of the target.
- `sip_address` (String) The SIP URI to which the call will be referred.
- `sip_auth_password` (String) SIP Authentication password used for SIP challenges.
- `sip_auth_username` (String) SIP Authentication username used for SIP challenges.



<a id="nestedatt--tools--retrieval"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.retrieval`

Optional:

- `bucket_ids` (List of String) List of [embedded storage buckets](https://developers.telnyx.com/api-reference/embeddings/embed-documents) to use for retrieval-augmented generation.
- `max_num_results` (Number) The maximum number of results to retrieve as context for the language model.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--send_message"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.send_message`

Optional:

- `message_template` (String) Optional message template with dynamic variable support using mustache syntax (e.g., {{variable_name}}). When set, the assistant will use this template for the SMS body instead of generating one. Dynamic variables like {{telnyx_end_user_target}}, {{telnyx_agent_target}}, and custom webhook-provided variables will be resolved at runtime.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--skip_turn"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.skip_turn`

Optional:

- `description` (String) The description of the function that will be passed to the assistant.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--transfer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.transfer`

Optional:

- `bridge_beep` (Attributes) Plays a short beep once the transfer completes and the calls are bridged, so the transfer destination knows the caller is now on the line. The warm transfer message plays before the bridge; this marks the moment the caller actually joins. Works with and without `warm_transfer_acceptance`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--transfer--bridge_beep))
- `custom_headers` (Attributes List) Custom headers to be added to the SIP INVITE for the transfer command. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--transfer--custom_headers))
- `description` (String) A description of the transfer tool. By default, Telnyx generates this automatically based on the configured targets. Typically only set when importing an assistant from another provider that allowed a custom description; in that case the provided value is preserved. Most users should leave this empty and let Telnyx manage it.
- `diversion` (String) The number the inbound call was received on, forwarded so an unverified non-Telnyx `from` can be used as the caller id -- typically to transfer out as the original caller by pairing `from: "{{telnyx_end_user_target}}"` with `diversion: "{{telnyx_agent_target}}"`. The caller id is only accepted while that number is still on an active inbound call to this `diversion` number, and the `diversion` number must be one you own or have verified.
- `from` (String) Number or SIP URI placing the call.
- `targets` (String) The different possible targets of the transfer. The assistant will be able to choose one of the targets to transfer the call to. This can also be a dynamic variable string like `{{ targets }}` where `targets` is returned by the dynamic variables webhook and resolves to an array of target objects at runtime. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `voicemail_detection` (Attributes) Configuration for voicemail detection (AMD - Answering Machine Detection) on the transferred call. Allows the assistant to detect when a voicemail system answers the transferred call and take appropriate action. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--transfer--voicemail_detection))
- `warm_message_delay_ms` (Number) Optional delay in milliseconds before playing the warm message audio when the transferred call is answered. When set, the audio_url is not included in the dial command; instead, playback starts after the specified delay. When not set, existing behavior (audio_url in dial) is preserved.
- `warm_transfer_acceptance` (Attributes) Requires the transfer destination to accept the call before the caller is bridged. When enabled, the assistant speaks privately with the destination after they answer — delivering the warm transfer message and asking whether they take the call — while the caller keeps hearing ringback. The assistant then finalizes the transfer with the built-in `complete_transfer` tool: an accept bridges the calls, a decline hangs up the destination and returns the assistant to the caller with the reason the destination gave. Requires either `warm_transfer_instructions` or a `message` on every target, otherwise the assistant fails to save. Only available for calls started with `ai_assistant_start`; single-caller conversations only (a conference or additional invited participants fall back to a regular warm transfer). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--transfer--warm_transfer_acceptance))
- `warm_transfer_instructions` (String) Natural language instructions for your agent for how to provide context for the transfer recipient.

<a id="nestedatt--tools--transfer--bridge_beep"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.transfer.bridge_beep`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether to play the beep when the calls are bridged.
- `target_legs` (String) Who hears the beep. `self` plays it to the transfer destination only; `both` plays it to the destination and the original caller. One of `both`, `self`.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--transfer--custom_headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.transfer.custom_headers`

Optional:

- `name` (String)
- `value` (String) The value of the header. Note that we support mustache templating for the value. For example you can use `{{#integration_secret}}test-secret{{/integration_secret}}` to pass the value of the integration secret.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--transfer--voicemail_detection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.transfer.voicemail_detection`

Optional:

- `detection_config` (String) Advanced AMD detection configuration parameters. All values are optional - Telnyx will use defaults if not specified. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `detection_mode` (String) The AMD detection mode to use. 'premium' enables premium answering machine detection. 'disabled' turns off AMD detection. One of `disabled`, `premium`.
- `on_voicemail_detected` (String) Action to take when voicemail is detected on the transferred call. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--transfer--warm_transfer_acceptance"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.transfer.warm_transfer_acceptance`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the destination must accept the transfer before the calls are bridged.
- `end_user_target_context_mode` (String) Controls whether the private exchange between the assistant and the transfer destination is kept out of the conversation. With `private` (default) the exchange never reaches the conversation history, AI conversations, webhooks or insights, and the transfer tool result is rewritten with the outcome only. With `shared` the exchange stays in the conversation like any other messages. One of `private`, `shared`.
- `require_acceptance` (Boolean) Fail closed when the acceptance consult cannot run. Off by default: if the consult cannot be set up for any reason — including where acceptance is unavailable at all (`gather_using_ai`, Conversation Relay or web calls, a conference, or additional invited participants) — the transfer degrades to a plain warm transfer (the warm transfer message is played to the destination as audio and the calls are bridged anyway). Set to true to treat those paths as a decline instead: the destination is disconnected without being asked, the assistant returns to the caller, and no bridge happens without an acceptance. Only consult-setup failures are affected; the destination must still explicitly accept on every consult that does run.
- `timeout_secs` (Number) How long, in seconds, the destination has to accept the transfer, counted from when the private consult starts (right after the destination answers, or after `warm_message_delay_ms`). The caller keeps hearing ringback the whole time. If no acceptance arrives in time, the destination is hung up and the assistant returns to the caller (the transfer fails as a timeout). Raise it for destinations that answer before a human is on the line, such as a call-center queue/ACD or an IVR playing hold audio; keep it as short as practical, since the caller waits on ringback until it expires.



<a id="nestedatt--tools--update_dynamic_variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.update_dynamic_variables`

Optional:

- `description` (String) Description of the tool passed to the assistant, guiding when to call it and which variables to update.
- `name` (String) The function name surfaced to the LLM. Must match the OpenAI function-name pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` and be unique across the assistant's function, webhook, and client_side tools.
- `updatable_variables` (Attributes List) The dynamic variables the assistant is allowed to write. At least one is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--update_dynamic_variables--updatable_variables))

<a id="nestedatt--tools--update_dynamic_variables--updatable_variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.update_dynamic_variables.updatable_variables`

Optional:

- `description` (String) Optional description of the variable, guiding the assistant on what value to capture.
- `name` (String) The dynamic-variable key to update. Must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$` and may not start with the reserved `telnyx_` prefix (reserved for system variables). The `pattern` encodes both rules via a negative lookahead.
- `type` (String) Optional hint for the variable's value type (e.g. `string`).



<a id="nestedatt--tools--vision"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.vision`

Optional:

- `max_frame_age_secs` (Number) Frames received longer ago than this many seconds are not shown to the assistant, so it never describes a frozen or disconnected camera as live.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--webhook"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.webhook`

Optional:

- `async` (Boolean) If async, the assistant will move forward without waiting for your server to respond.
- `async_timeout_ms` (Number) Maximum time in milliseconds that the conversation worker waits for an async webhook response before returning "Submitted" to the LLM. If unset, the platform default (currently 300ms) is used.
- `body_parameters` (Attributes) The body parameters the webhook tool accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. These parameters will be passed to the webhook as the body of the request. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--webhook--body_parameters))
- `description` (String) The description of the tool.
- `headers` (Attributes List) The headers to be sent to the external tool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--webhook--headers))
- `messages` (Attributes List) Filler messages spoken while a synchronous webhook request is in progress. `request_start` messages are spoken immediately when the request begins. `request_response_delayed` messages are spoken after `timing_ms` has elapsed only if the webhook response is still pending. Filler messages are not used for asynchronous webhooks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--webhook--messages))
- `method` (String) The HTTP method to be used when calling the external tool. One of `DELETE`, `GET`, `PATCH`, `POST`, `PUT`.
- `name` (String) The name of the tool.
- `path_parameters` (Attributes) The path parameters the webhook tool accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. These parameters will be passed to the webhook as the path of the request if the URL contains a placeholder for a value. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--webhook--path_parameters))
- `preset_body_fields` (String) Body fields supplied by the assistant configuration rather than by the model. They are never advertised in the tool definition, so the LLM can neither see nor set them, and they take precedence over a `body_parameters` value of the same name. Values support mustache templating, so they can hold dynamic variables (`{{customer_id}}`) and integration secrets (`{{#integration_secret}}my-secret{{/integration_secret}}`). Not sent on `GET` requests, which carry no body. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `preset_query_params` (String) Query string parameters supplied by the assistant configuration rather than by the model. They are never advertised in the tool definition, so the LLM can neither see nor set them, and they take precedence over a `query_parameters` value of the same name. Values support mustache templating, so they can hold dynamic variables (`{{telnyx_end_user_target}}`) and integration secrets (`{{#integration_secret}}my-secret{{/integration_secret}}`). Unlike values templated directly into the `url`, these are percent-encoded, so a value such as `+15551234567` survives the round trip. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `query_parameters` (Attributes) The query parameters the webhook tool accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. These parameters will be passed to the webhook as the query of the request. See the [JSON Schema reference](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema) for documentation about the format (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--webhook--query_parameters))
- `store_fields_as_variables` (Attributes List) A list of mappings that extract values from the webhook response and store them as dynamic variables. Each mapping specifies a dynamic variable name and a dot-notation path to the value in the response body. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools--webhook--store_fields_as_variables))
- `url` (String) The URL of the external tool to be called. This URL is going to be used by the assistant. The URL can be templated like: `https://example.com/api/v1/{id}`, where `{id}` is a placeholder for a value that will be provided by the assistant if `path_parameters` are provided with the `id` attribute.

<a id="nestedatt--tools--webhook--body_parameters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.webhook.body_parameters`

Optional:

- `properties` (String) The properties of the body parameters. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `required` (List of String) The required properties of the body parameters.
- `type` (String) One of `object`.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--webhook--headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.webhook.headers`

Optional:

- `name` (String)
- `value` (String) The value of the header. Note that we support mustache templating for the value. For example you can use `Bearer {{#integration_secret}}test-secret{{/integration_secret}}` to pass the value of the integration secret as the bearer token. [Telnyx signature headers](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/voice/programmable-voice/voice-api-webhooks) will be automatically added to the request.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--webhook--messages"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.webhook.messages`

Optional:

- `content` (String) The text the assistant speaks.
- `timing_ms` (Number) The delay in milliseconds from the start of the webhook request.
- `type` (String) One of `request_response_delayed`, `request_start`.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--webhook--path_parameters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.webhook.path_parameters`

Optional:

- `properties` (String) The properties of the path parameters. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `required` (List of String) The required properties of the path parameters.
- `type` (String) One of `object`.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--webhook--query_parameters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.webhook.query_parameters`

Optional:

- `properties` (String) The properties of the query parameters. A JSON document; use `jsonencode()`.
- `required` (List of String) The required properties of the query parameters.
- `type` (String) One of `object`.


<a id="nestedatt--tools--webhook--store_fields_as_variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools.webhook.store_fields_as_variables`

Optional:

- `name` (String) The name of the dynamic variable to store the extracted value in.
- `value_path` (String) A dot-notation path to the value in the webhook response body (e.g. 'customer.name' or 'id').




<a id="nestedatt--transcription"></a>
### Nested Schema for `transcription`

Optional:

- `api_key_ref` (String) Integration secret identifier for the transcription provider API key. Currently used for Azure transcription regions that require a customer-provided API key.
- `challenger` (Attributes) The language booster: a second model that transcribes alongside `model`, and the rule that decides which transcript the assistant uses. Both models must be streaming, or both non-streaming, and, except with `merge_words`, `model` must support `language` alongside another model (for example, `cohere/ar-stt` supports only `ar` there). If the language booster can't run, the call runs on `model` alone; if either model fails mid-call, the call continues on the other. On update, omit the field to keep the stored language booster, or send `null` to remove it. When an update changes `model` or `language` and the stored language booster no longer fits, it is removed without an error. Can't be combined with `fallback_models`; to replace stored fallbacks, send `fallback_models: []` in the same request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transcription--challenger))
- `fallback_models` (Attributes List) Up to 3 streaming models that take over transcription, in this order, when the model in use fails, at the start of a call or mid-call. `model` must be a streaming model too, and must support `language` alongside other models. On update, a list replaces the stored one: omit the field to keep the stored list, or send `null` or `[]` to remove it. When an update changes `model` or `language`, stored fallbacks that no longer fit are removed without an error. Can't be combined with `challenger`, the language booster; to replace a stored language booster, send `challenger: null` in the same request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transcription--fallback_models))
- `language` (String) The language of the audio to be transcribed. If not set, or if set to `auto`, supported models will automatically detect the language. For `deepgram/flux`, supported values are: `auto` (Telnyx language detection controls the language hint), `multi` (no language hint), and language-specific hints `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, `hi`, `ru`, `pt`, `ja`, `it`, and `nl`. For `soniox/stt-rt-v4` and `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `auto` omits the language hint and lets Soniox auto-detect; ISO 639-1 codes (e.g. `en`, `es`) bias detection toward that language; `settings.language_hints` can pin multiple languages at once instead. For `humain/realtime`, supported values are `ar`, `en`, `codeswitch` (Arabic/English code-switching), and `auto` (resolves server-side to code-switching). Unlike other models, `humain/realtime` does not fall back to `auto` when `language` is omitted — omitting it applies `en` instead. For `reson8/turns`, supported values are `auto` (or unset) for automatic language detection, and the language codes `nl`, `en`, `fr`, `fy`, `de`, `it`, `pl`, `pt`, `es`, and `sv` to fix the transcription language. For `cohere/ar-stt`, supported values are `ar` and `en`; unlike other models, this model does not auto-detect and defaults to `ar` when `language` is omitted. For `speechmatics/linden-1`, there is no auto-detect; set a code from Speechmatics' Realtime language list (67 language codes, including `es-bilingual-en` for Spanish and English bilingual, and the spelling and script variants `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-AU`, `cmn-Hans`, and `cmn-Hant`; `en` alone uses the default spelling); unset defaults to `en`, while an explicit `auto`, `auto_beta`, or `multi` is rejected with a 400.
- `model` (String) The speech to text model to be used by the voice assistant. All Deepgram models are run on-premise. - `deepgram/flux` is optimized for turn-taking with multilingual language hints. - `deepgram/nova-3` is multilingual with automatic language detection. - `deepgram/nova-2` is Deepgram's previous-generation multilingual model. - `speechmatics/standard` is a Speechmatics model self-hosted by Telnyx; it supports a fixed set of language packs (including bilingual packs such as `ar_en`) and defaults to `en`. - `speechmatics/linden-1` (preview) is a vendor-hosted streaming model with no auto-detect; set `language` from Speechmatics' Realtime language list (defaults to `en`). - `azure/fast` is a multilingual Azure transcription model. - `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` (AssemblyAI Universal-3.6 Pro) is a multilingual streaming model with configurable turn detection. The legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming` are still accepted and run the same model. - `xai/grok-stt` is a multilingual Grok STT model. - `soniox/stt-rt-v4` and `soniox/stt-rt-v5` are multilingual streaming models with automatic language detection, configurable endpointing, term biasing (`context`), and `language_hints`. - `nvidia/parakeet-v3` is a multilingual transcription model with automatic language detection. - `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1` is an English-only medical transcription model (Parakeet-based). - `humain/realtime` is a streaming model with native Arabic and Arabic/English code-switching support. - `reson8/turns` is a turn-based streaming model covering 10 European languages with automatic language detection. - `cohere/ar-stt` is a non-streaming Arabic and English transcription model. - `telnyx/basira` is a non-streaming Arabic transcription model. One of `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro`, `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro`, `assemblyai/universal-streaming`, `azure/fast`, `cohere/ar-stt`, `deepgram/flux`, `deepgram/nova-2`, `deepgram/nova-3`, `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2`, `humain/realtime`, `nvidia/parakeet-v3`, `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1`, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, `reson8/turns`, `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `speechmatics/linden-1`, `speechmatics/standard`, `telnyx/basira`, `xai/grok-stt`.
- `region` (String) Region on third party cloud providers (currently Azure) if using one of their models. Some regions require `api_key_ref`.
- `settings` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transcription--settings))

<a id="nestedatt--transcription--challenger"></a>
### Nested Schema for `transcription.challenger`

Optional:

- `language` (String) The language this model transcribes. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the language of `transcription.model`. The request is rejected when this model doesn't support the language it would run. It is also rejected when it would run the same model on the same language as `transcription.model`.
- `model` (String) The language booster's model. It must be the same kind of model as `transcription.model`: both streaming (`deepgram/flux`, `deepgram/nova-3`, `deepgram/nova-2`, `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` or its legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming`, `xai/grok-stt`, `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `humain/realtime`, `reson8/turns`) or both non-streaming (`azure/fast`, `nvidia/parakeet-v3`, `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1`, `cohere/ar-stt`, `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2`, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, `telnyx/basira`). It can be the same model as `transcription.model` on a different `language`. One of `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro`, `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro`, `assemblyai/universal-streaming`, `azure/fast`, `cohere/ar-stt`, `deepgram/flux`, `deepgram/nova-2`, `deepgram/nova-3`, `distil-whisper/distil-large-v2`, `humain/realtime`, `nvidia/parakeet-v3`, `omi-health/omi-med-stt-v1`, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, `reson8/turns`, `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `telnyx/basira`, `xai/grok-stt`.
- `rule` (String) How the assistant picks the transcript it uses. The models are compared on how complete and confident their transcripts are, not on language, so the rules work best when both models understand the callers' language. - `best_turn` (default): both models transcribe the whole call. Each turn uses the language booster's transcript only when it scores higher than the transcript of `transcription.model` (clearly higher with non-streaming models). With streaming models, `transcription.model` also decides when each turn ends. Available for every pair. - `best_engine`: both models transcribe the first turns, then the call continues alone on the model whose transcripts scored higher. If neither clearly leads, `transcription.model` continues. Streaming models only. - `merge_words`: both models transcribe each utterance and their words are merged, keeping Arabic and English spoken in the same sentence. Available only for `telnyx/basira` with `cohere/ar-stt`, in either order. The pair runs on the language that applies to `telnyx/basira` (its own, or that of `transcription.model`), which must be Arabic (`ar` or an `ar-` locale), `multi`, or `auto`. One of `best_engine`, `best_turn`, `merge_words`.
- `settings` (Attributes) Settings for the language booster, with the same fields and limits as `transcription.settings`. Fields that don't apply to this model's provider are dropped, and the provider's defaults fill in the rest. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the settings of `transcription.model` where they apply to this model. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transcription--challenger--settings))

<a id="nestedatt--transcription--challenger--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `transcription.challenger.settings`

Optional:

- `context` (String) Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. A comma-separated list of terms to boost for recognition during transcription, for staff names, building names, or other domain-specific vocabulary. This field may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) using mustache syntax (e.g. `Telnyx,{{customer_name}},VoIP`). Variables are resolved at call time before the value is sent to Soniox.
- `eager_eot_threshold` (Number) Available only for deepgram/flux. Confidence threshold for eager end of turn detection. Must be lower than or equal to eot_threshold. Setting this equal to eot_threshold effectively disables eager end of turn.
- `enable_endpoint_detection` (Boolean) Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. When true, Soniox emits end-of-utterance events at the cadence configured by `max_endpoint_delay_ms`.
- `end_of_turn_confidence_threshold` (Number, Deprecated) Deprecated and ignored. Accepted for backwards compatibility. AssemblyAI turn detection is configured with min_turn_silence and max_turn_silence.
- `eot_threshold` (Number) Available only for deepgram/flux. Confidence required to trigger an end of turn. Higher values = more reliable turn detection but slightly increased latency.
- `eot_timeout_ms` (Number) Available only for deepgram/flux. Maximum milliseconds of silence before forcing an end of turn, regardless of confidence.
- `interim_results` (Boolean) Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. When true, Soniox streams interim (non-final) results in addition to finalized transcripts.
- `keyterm` (String) A comma-separated list of key terms to boost for recognition during transcription, used by Deepgram, Reson8, Speechmatics Linden 1 and AssemblyAI models. Helps improve accuracy for domain-specific terminology, proper nouns, or uncommon words. At most 1000 characters in total. For assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming), also at most 100 terms of up to 50 characters each. This field may be templated with [dynamic variables](https://developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) using mustache syntax (e.g. `Telnyx,{{customer_name}},VoIP`). Variables are resolved at call time before the value is sent to the speech-to-text engine.
- `language_hints` (List of String) Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. A list of ISO 639-1 language codes (e.g. `["nl", "fr"]`) to pin recognition to multiple languages at once, overriding the single hint derived from `language`.
- `max_endpoint_delay_ms` (Number) Available only for soniox/stt-rt-v4 and soniox/stt-rt-v5. Maximum silence (in milliseconds) before Soniox emits an end-of-utterance event. Only honored when `enable_endpoint_detection` is true.
- `max_turn_silence` (Number) Available only for assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming). Maximum duration of silence in milliseconds before forcing an end of turn.
- `min_turn_silence` (Number) Available only for assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming). Minimum duration of silence in milliseconds before a turn can end. Must be less than or equal to max_turn_silence.
- `numerals` (Boolean)
- `prompt` (String) Available only for assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro (and its legacy aliases assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro and assemblyai/universal-streaming). Context about the conversation (domain, names, terms) to improve transcription; describe the content, do not give instructions. Leave empty unless needed. At most 1750 characters.
- `remove_disfluencies` (Boolean) Available only for speechmatics/linden-1. When true, filler words such as "um" and "uh" are removed from the transcript. Disfluency removal is supported only for `ar`, `cmn`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `he`, `hi`, `hu`, `it`, `ja`, `nl`, `pl`, `pt`, and `ru`, determined by the base language (so `en-US`, `en-GB`, `en-AU`, `cmn-Hans`, and `cmn-Hant` are supported); for other languages, filler words remain in the transcript.
- `smart_format` (Boolean)



<a id="nestedatt--transcription--fallback_models"></a>
### Nested Schema for `transcription.fallback_models`

Optional:

- `language` (String) The language the fallback transcribes. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the language of `transcription.model`. The request is rejected when the fallback model doesn't support the language it would run.
- `model` (String) The fallback model. It must be a streaming model other than `transcription.model` and the other fallbacks: `deepgram/flux`, `deepgram/nova-3`, `deepgram/nova-2`, `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro` (or its legacy aliases `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro` and `assemblyai/universal-streaming`), `xai/grok-stt`, `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `humain/realtime`, or `reson8/turns`. One of `assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro`, `assemblyai/universal-3-6-pro`, `assemblyai/universal-streaming`, `deepgram/flux`, `deepgram/nova-2`, `deepgram/nova-3`, `humain/realtime`, `reson8/turns`, `soniox/stt-rt-v4`, `soniox/stt-rt-v5`, `xai/grok-stt`.
- `settings` (Attributes) Settings for the fallback, with the same fields and limits as `transcription.settings`. Fields that don't apply to this model's provider are dropped, and the provider's defaults fill in the rest. Omit it or set it to `null` to use the settings of `transcription.model` where they apply to this model. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transcription--fallback_models--settings))
